description: Cross-binding conformance for how far an `operator_compose` merged-away rename REACHES (esm-libraries-spec §4.7.1 step 4). A renaming match — a `translate` match, or the bare-name fallback #216 resolves by ownership — folds `B.x` into `A.x`, so `B.x` is DELETED and every equation in the document is rewritten off the dead spelling. That rewrite is document-wide over EQUATION ASTs and nothing else, and three other places address the state BY NAME: a `couple` connector's `from`/`to` and a `variable_map`'s `from`/`to`, which are plain scoped-reference STRINGS on the entry object; the override keys a runner is handed; and a surviving expression-template registry body. §4.7.5 step 3 applies every `operator_compose` BEFORE any `couple` or `variable_map`, so an entry that has not run yet can still name a spelling the merge has already deleted. The decision this category pins is RESOLUTION, not refusal: a reference to a merged-away name resolves to the survivor, so a document that merges `B.x` onto `A.x` stays addressable by either spelling. Refusing instead would be defensible for a name nothing can resolve, but these are renames the author ASKED for — a `translate` map names the surviving spelling on purpose — and a document is built around them. Like `operator_compose_merge` and `override_key_diagnostics` this category carries no golden: what it pins is REACH, asserted as structure (which names survive, which equations reference what) rather than as numbers.

flatten._comment: The rewrite is a pure structural transform, so a rewrite-only port implements it in full. All five bindings are in scope.

override_keys._comment: The runner half: a caller's `initial_conditions` / `parameter_overrides` key naming the deleted spelling. Only the three EXECUTING bindings have an override-key surface at all — the same scope split `override_key_diagnostics` records.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no override-key surface
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no override-key surface

output_selection._comment: The OUTPUT half: a name-keyed READ of a finished run. Scope is narrower than `override_keys` and the reasons differ per binding, so each is recorded. What is pinned is that the READ resolves, not that the row NAMES change — resolving a read must never invent a name the flattened system does not declare.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no result object to read by name
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no result object to read by name
scope_excluded.julia: the result is a SciML `ODESolution` indexed through SciMLBase's own `SymbolCache`: the package FILLS that name list (`_symbol_cache`) but does not own the lookup, so resolving a merged-away spelling there needs a custom SymbolicIndexingInterface system type. The problem-side name lookup this binding DOES own, `observed_field(prob, name)`, resolves through `EsmProblem.merged_renames`. Tracked in EarthSciML/EarthSciAST#271.

not_covered_in_any_binding.derive_output_plan: The exported output-plan function takes the request list and the slot names and nothing else, in both Julia and Rust. Resolving a merged-away request INSIDE it needs a new parameter on a function `output_derivation` (§5.17) pins as a cross-binding surface, so every in-repo caller resolves at the CALL SITE instead (Rust's `esm simulate --format grid`, and `SolveOptions.output_observed` before the solve). An EXTERNAL caller passing a merged-away name straight to `derive_output_plan` is therefore still on its own. Julia's `_match_requested!` happens to tolerate the common case anyway, because it matches bare tails both ways. Tracked, with the Julia solution-read half it shares a cause with, in EarthSciML/EarthSciAST#271.

events_and_updates._comment: The name-keyed places that are NOT equations and NOT coupling entries: a discrete/continuous event (its affect `lhs` is a plain NAME string, its affect `rhs`, its conditions, and a `condition` trigger's expression) and a variable's `update` rules (`when` / `expression`, carried on the VARIABLE rather than in `equations`). Both are pure structural rewrites over the flattened form, so all five bindings implement them in full. Where a binding namespaces events at COLLECTION -- before any coupling rule runs -- the dead spelling survives fully qualified; where it namespaces them after coupling, the reference finds no live variable and is left bare. Both are an affect writing to an unknown the flattened system does not declare.

template_registry._comment: The ONE surface that REFUSES rather than resolves. A surviving `expression_templates` body is a shadow copy of authored source that no equation walk reaches and that expands at the BUILD boundary, so a body naming a merged-away state would expand later and elsewhere into a variable the flattened system does not declare. Rewriting it would make the flattened registry disagree with the expand-at-load image the same document produces, which esm-spec 9.6.4 rule 2 requires to be observably identical -- so the document is refused at flatten instead. A template `param` shadows the outer name (9.6.1), so a body that BINDS the name is fine; the fixture deliberately does not.

inline_tests._comment: A component's own inline test addresses the quantity by its LOCAL name (esm-spec 6.6), in an assertion and in an `initial_conditions` key. A merge can fold that component's state onto another's, and then neither resolves. The two halves fail differently: the assertion fails LOUDLY (`scalar state 'O3' not found`), while the IC key is dropped in SILENCE and the state runs from the survivor's declared default -- a wrong answer rather than a missing one. Only the three bindings that RUN inline tests are in scope.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no inline-test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no inline-test runner

merged_variable_renames_field._comment: The map flatten records on its metadata so a consumer that addresses a state by name can resolve a spelling the merge moved. Named per binding; the CONTENT is the cross-binding contract.

cases.note: The QUIET failure. A `couple` connector targets `Sink.O3`, which the earlier compose deleted; the connector's `to` is a plain string the equation retarget never reaches, so the target matched nothing and the whole connector was dropped — leaving a flattened tendency arithmetically identical to a document with no `couple` entry at all. `Emis.flux` in `D(Chem.O3, t)` is what the fix is observable as.

The LOUD failure, and the sharper half. A later `variable_map` names the deleted `Sink.O3` as its `from`, so the substitution injected a name the flattened system no longer declares into every equation referencing `Consumer.bg` — a dangling reference that surfaces far downstream as an unbound variable at the build boundary, not a missing term.

The `variable_map` EXPRESSION arm (esm-spec §10.4), which the `later_variable_map` case does not reach — that one drives a NAMED transform. The two arms are implemented differently on purpose: a named transform substitutes `to` away, so the entry's endpoints must be resolved before it runs, while an expression transform installs its node as the defining equation of the observed it introduces. A binding that installs that node at COLLECTION has already had the document-wide equation retarget rewrite it, and resolving the entry's `from` as well would break the §10.4 `contains` check against the AUTHORED node. Different routes, one observable result — which is exactly what a conformance case should pin, and what nothing pinned before: `Consumer.bg` is defined over `Chem.ozone`, and `Sink.O3` survives nowhere.

A caller's initial-condition key naming the deleted spelling. Unresolved it designates nothing: the key is silently dropped (Python, Julia) or reported unknown (Rust), and the state runs from its declared 30.0 — a wrong answer, not a missing one, because the run still reports a verdict. `parameter_overrides` shares this canonicalization, but a merged-away name is always a DEPENDENT VARIABLE (a state or an observed) and never a parameter, so the state side is where the case actually lands.

A caller reading the finished run by the deleted spelling. The trajectory it names MOVED to `Chem.O3`'s row, so the read resolves there rather than reporting a variable that never existed — and the row NAMES still report only the surviving spelling, because resolving a read must not invent a name the flattened system does not declare. Where a binding also takes an output REQUEST (an `output_observed` / `--observed` list, an `observed_field` lookup), the same map resolves it before the plan is derived.

The `translate` renames ACROSS differing local names, which is what makes this case load-bearing: the survivor is `Chem.ozone`, so nothing in the flattened system is spelled `O3` and the bare-name coincidence that rescues a same-local-name merge cannot apply. The affect's `lhs` is the sharpest half -- it is a plain name STRING, so a walk that maps only EXPRESSIONS leaves it holding the dead spelling even after the affect's own RHS has been rewritten.

Flatten must REFUSE. The body references the component's local `O3`, which scopes to `Sink.O3` and which the merge then deletes; `O3` is not one of the template's `params`, so the 9.6.1 shadow does not apply. A binding that resolves here instead of refusing is as wrong as one that does nothing: it would silently rewrite authored source.

Both halves are pinned by one assertion. That it RESOLVES at all is the assertion half -- unresolved it raises `scalar state 'O3' not found`. That the actual is 10.0 rather than 30.0 is the `initial_conditions` half: the survivor's declared default is 30.0, so an IC key that failed to resolve would leave the run there and the test would still return a verdict. Both rates are zero, so the trajectory holds its initial value and the assertion reads the override rather than any integration.
